scope: one real skull-stripped T1, the same MNI152 2-mm brain reference and saved initial FLIRT affine for FSL FNIRT and FNIT

default.fnit_command: python -m fnit.fnirt --in T1_brain.nii.gz --ref MNI152_2mm_brain.nii.gz --aff initial.mat --config default --cout fnit_coeff.nii.gz --iout fnit_warped.nii.gz

global_linear_ablation.change: set --intmod=global_linear in both FSL and FNIT; all other command inputs and settings unchanged

fnit_polynomial_order_ablation.change: set FNIT --intorder 4; compare with the unchanged FSL default

source_findings: FSL includes deformation, global polynomial and local bias field in the same optimization parameter vector and gradient; FNIT fits polynomial and bias once before each deformation level and freezes them during that level.
FSL intorder=5 creates five polynomial coefficients (powers 0 through 4); FNIT intensity_order=5 currently creates six (powers 0 through 5).
interpretation: The nonlinear intensity-plus-bias branch is the dominant source of default T1 warp divergence in this case. The polynomial coefficient-count discrepancy is real but changing it alone has a small effect. The remaining global-linear difference and FNIT iout/coeff re-warp discrepancy mean numerical equivalence above r=0.9999 has not been demonstrated.
limits: Single real T1. FSL wrote gzip-valid, finite images but returned 255, so its output is a conditional numerical reference. CPU and GPU wall times are not a controlled speed comparison. No private image or voxelwise result is included.
